required_outcomes: Records the landlord's decision as approval of the rubbish and builders' waste clearance only, capped at £600 including VAT, and records that levelling and gravel are declined.

Takes the clearance forward through the route already in progress (Oakley and her contractor), passing on the £600 all-in cap and asking for a firm price within it and dates; does not bring in a second contractor in parallel.
Tells the tenant the clearance is approved and the contractor will be in touch to arrange access, that the landlord has decided not to level or gravel the garden, and gives no works date.
Does not escalate: the landlord's decision is clear and within what he was asked.
acceptable_alternatives: Returning the ticket to auto mode for provider selection when no contractor is on file, provided the £600 cap and the clearance-only scope are recorded.
Confirming the decision back to the landlord briefly.
positive_behaviours: Thanks the landlord and confirms the cap and scope back to him.
Explains to the tenant, without promising anything, that levelling and gravel are improvements the landlord is not obliged to make.
Asks the contractor for proof of proper disposal (a waste transfer note) with the invoice, given the specialist material.
red_flags: Asking the landlord to approve again, or putting the request back on hold for him.
Leaving the tenant without an update.
prohibited_actions: Instructing levelling or gravel, or any spend above £600 including VAT.
Giving the tenant a works date that nothing in the record supports.
critical_failures: Leaving the approved clearance with nobody instructed and nothing returned to provider selection, so the job stalls again.
